title: Patients’ Handling of Sensitive Health Data During Everyday Use of Large Language Models for Medical Questions
summary:
More and more people are using AI chatbots such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, or Microsoft Copilot to ask medical or health-related questions. These questions may concern symptoms, medical reports, medication, diagnoses, or conversations with doctors.

To receive more helpful or more personalized answers, some people may enter personal or health-related information into such programs. This may include symptoms, pre-existing conditions, medication, laboratory values, medical letters, or other sensitive health data. However, little is currently known about which types of information people actually enter and how they weigh potential benefits against data protection risks.

This study therefore aims to investigate whether and how people use AI chatbots for medical or health-related questions, which personal or health-related information they provide, and what role trust, expected benefit, and data protection concerns play in this context.

Participation is voluntary and anonymous via an online questionnaire. No names, contact details, or other directly identifying information will be collected. Completing the questionnaire takes approximately 10 to 15 minutes.
conditions: Use and risks of LLM in the medical field

interventions.name: Observational group: Participants in an anonymous web-based cross-sectional survey on the use of AI chatbots or large language models for medical or health-related questions and on the handling of personal or sensitive health data. No intervention is performed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with a current or past medical condition
- Ability to give independent informed consent
- Sufficient language skills to communicate and understand the study information
- Willingness to take part in an anonymous survey
Exclusion criteria:
- age < 18 Jahre
- Inability to give informed consent
- Inadequate understanding of the study information
- Acute emergencies or time-critical examinations
- Acute mental or cognitive impairment that precludes participation
